question: When a company opens a bank account, how does the bank decide who the real owner behind it is?
your_answer: It must identify the natural person(s) with controlling ownership — more than 10% of shares/capital/profits for a company — or who control it through other means; if no one qualifies, the senior managing official. Companies listed on stock exchanges (and their subsidiaries) are exempt from this identification.

question: Do banks apply extra checks when a foreign public official or someone from their family opens an account?
your_answer: Yes — for such persons (PEPs: people entrusted with prominent public functions BY A FOREIGN COUNTRY), the bank must have systems to identify them, establish their source of funds/wealth, take senior management approval for the account, and monitor it intensively — the same applies to family members and close associates.

question: At what ownership percentage does someone become the beneficial owner of a company, and is the threshold the same for an unincorporated association?
your_answer: No — for a company (and for a partnership) it is MORE THAN 10% of shares/capital/profits; for an unincorporated association or body of individuals it is MORE THAN 15%. For trusts: author, trustee, and beneficiaries with 10% or more interest.

question: What technical safeguards must a bank's V-CIP infrastructure have?
